name: Dyna-Q
analogy: Think of it as a trader who keeps a ledger of every situation he has seen and how each choice turned out. After every real bar, instead of waiting for the next one, he spends a few minutes replaying entries from the ledger, so one real experience teaches him dozens of times.

steps.title: Sort the market into a small number of cells
steps.description: A handful of features are each cut into a few ranges, and the combination of ranges names a cell. The whole market is reduced to a modest table of situations.
steps.inExample: The relative strength index, the volume ratio and the 5-bar trend are each cut into 5 ranges, so there are 125 cells.

steps.title: Keep a table of what each action is worth
steps.description: For every cell and every position (long, flat, short) the table holds a number: how much reward the agent expects from taking that position there and acting well afterwards.
steps.inExample: In cell 16 the table says long is worth 3 ticks, flat 0 ticks and short minus 2 ticks, where a tick is a quarter of an index point.

steps.title: Learn from the real bar
steps.description: After a real bar closes, the table entry for the action taken is corrected by the gap between what it predicted and what the reward plus next cell's value suggest.
steps.inExample: Going long in cell 16 paid 4 ticks, a little more than the 3 expected, so its worth rises slightly.

steps.title: Remember what happened
steps.description: A second table records, for each cell and action, the last reward and next cell that followed. This is the agent's memory of how the market behaves.
steps.inExample: The memory notes that from cell 16 going long was followed by cell 37 and a reward of 4 ticks.

steps.title: Replay remembered experiences between bars
steps.description: A fixed number of past cell and action pairs are picked at random, looked up in the memory and put through the same correction. One real bar therefore produces many corrections.
steps.inExample: With 20 planning steps per real bar, 20 remembered pairs are replayed after the 14:05 bar.

steps.title: Choose the action with the highest worth
steps.description: To act, the agent finds the cell the market is in and takes the position with the highest worth, with occasional random choices early on so it keeps exploring.
steps.inExample: For the newest bar, the cell is 16 and the highest worth is long at 3 ticks.

useFor.task: A quick, readable baseline for a position policy
useFor.example: Learning a long, flat or short rule from three binned indicators on 5-minute MNQ bars that can be read straight off a table.
Getting more from a few thousand bars of a thinly traded contract by replaying them many times.

useFor.task: Re-checking the table after a regime shift
useFor.example: Using the version that favours long-unvisited cells so the agent re-tests a rule that may have stopped working.

useFor.task: Teaching how planning and learning combine
useFor.example: Showing a colleague how one real transition becomes many learning steps.
Looking up a position in a small table in constant time for every 1-minute bar.

avoidWhen: The signal depends on many continuous features at once; a table of cells cannot hold them, and a tree model or neural network handles continuous inputs naturally.
The market's response is very noisy; the remembered last outcome for each cell is unreliable, and the replays just repeat noise.

example.scenario: After training on a year of five-minute MNQ bars, Dyna-Q is asked what to do at 14:05. The bar is mapped to a cell of the table and the position with the highest learned worth is chosen.

input.summary: The newest bar mapped to a cell of binned features, and the learned table.

fields.name: relative strength index, 14 bars
fields.meaning: A momentum reading from 0 to 100, placed in the lowest range.

fields.name: volume against its 20-bar average
fields.meaning: How heavy trading was compared with the recent norm.

fields.name: return over the last 5 bars
fields.value: down about a third of a percent (range 1 of 5)
fields.meaning: How much price has fallen over the previous 25 minutes.

fields.name: cell number
fields.meaning: The label of the combination of the three ranges.

fields.name: planning steps per real bar
fields.meaning: How many remembered experiences are replayed after each real bar.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The price at which the newest bar closed, rounded to the nearest point.

output.summary: The learned worth of each position in the cell and the chosen action.

fields.name: worth of long
fields.meaning: The reward the table expects from going long in this cell, in quarter-point ticks.

fields.name: worth of flat
fields.meaning: The reward the table expects from staying out.

fields.name: worth of short
fields.meaning: The reward the table expects from going short in this cell.

fields.name: chosen action
fields.meaning: The position with the highest worth.

example.reading: Check how many cells actually prefer something other than flat: a table that prefers flat everywhere has only learned that trading costs money. A cell the table never visited reads as zero worth for everything, so do not trust a long call there.
